issues.title: Validate tracker features.
test
Add support for multiple status and priority filters, like labels.
Give short aliases for the flags, i.e. `-p --priority`, etc.
Add support for `--label-append` and `--label-remove` commands to append labels or remove them completely.
Sort the issues with a status of `done` to the bottom of their priority bracket by default.`

Only show issues with status `open` and `in-progress` in the default list. Exclude `done` and `closed`. If any other filter is applied that is *not* status, it should show all matches except for `closed`. `closed` is a special case. Filtering by label, or priority should return all `open`,`in-progress`, and `done` items that match.
Long issue titles should wrap in the column, or we can add a description field only visible on `tracker show <id>` and an indicator in the list view.
Status should be progressive/validated. Right now, it's set to `open` on create, but update might allow it to be set to arbitrary values.
`tracker_dir()` panics instead of propagating an error. It needs error handling like the rest of the codebase.
`save_issuse()` is a non-atomic write. It truncates the file and writes in place. Perferred behavior is to use a temp file and `fs::rename()`

IDs are reused after deletion.  The IDs are reused based on the highest numbered current issue, not counting deletions.  This could cause references to a deleted issue to point to a new issue instead.  I think that two things would be good here.  1. Add a counter object to track the highest issue number so far.  2. Favoring `closed` status over deletion.  I would rather actually have all the issues not be deleted for record keeping, and use the `closed` status to denote issues that will not be persued.

The `description` field is completeley inacessible from the CLI.  This is a signficant oversight.  There's no way to touch the description, and that's part of the data that we want.  I would also like to add the capability to open the description in a text editor, given that.

Labels are not normalized to lowercase on storage, making everything case-sensitive and inconsistent.  Labels aren't sanitized and the filtering is strict, so that can cause issues of mismatch.  I would prefer to normalize on entry.

`Priority`'s sort order is encoded silently in declaration order.  This is true and it assumes a fixed list of priority levels, while the flag takes any string.  Perhaps, limiting the priority levels to a set of inputs, with tab completion would work better?  Or reading a config file that declares them?

`Priority`'s sort order is encoded silently in declaration order. If anyone adds a Critical variant or rearranges the enum for any reason, the sort silently breaks. The Ord implementation for a type that has a meaningful semantic order should be explicit, not derived, or at minimum it should have a comment stating the invariant.
Add `critical` priority at higher sort than `high`.
Add tab completions for bash, zsh, fish, and nushell for priority levels.
`--title` and `--description` are missing from `update`.
`--label` on `update` is silently destructive and the help text doesn't warn about it.  Add a warning to the help text.
Add the ability to append labels, and also to clear all current labels in the update interface.
`cmd_delete` has no `--yes`/`--force` flag for scripted use.  Add one.
The tracker does not search parent directory, only the current directory.  Other project scoped tools walk up the directory structure to find the root, and tracker should do that too.

`status_str` is redundant with the `clap::ValueEnum` derivation. `main.rs:84-91`: `status_str` manually maps each `Status` variant to a string. These strings are identical to the ones `clap` already derives from `#[serde(rename_all = snake_case)]` and `#[value(name = in-progress)]`. There are now two places to update if a variant is renamed. Remove `status_str` and implement `Display` on `Status` instead, or at minimum have `status_colored` call into the `ValueEnum` trait.
`cmd_show` label is `Desc:` (truncated) which is inconsistent with the field name.  It's also the only field that's truncated.  I would prefer in not truncated.
There's no `updated_at` field, and that would be useful.

The magic number `12` in `cmd_list` for status column padding is unexplained.  It's the correct size for the current `status` options, but making it dynamic to the widest status means that it will work properly with any changes to the list of `status` options in the future.
There are no tests.  We should use Rust's built in test harness.

Piping tracker output into a closed pipe (e.g. `tracker list | head`) panics with `failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe` instead of exiting cleanly. Println macros panic on EPIPE; the CLI should treat a broken stdout pipe as a normal exit.

The priority column in cmd_list uses a hardcoded `{:<8}` width, and the priority name strings ("critical", "high", "medium", "low") are hardcoded in both cmd_list and cmd_show, duplicating the clap ValueEnum names just like the old status_str. Implement Display on Priority (via ValueEnum, using f.pad), add a priority_colored helper to de-duplicate the color match, and derive the column width dynamically from the widest name — mirroring the #24/#27 fix for Status.
Issues are marked as updated on creation
issues.description: Issues are marked as updated on creation, which is incorrect.  It conveys information that isn't intended.  It's also verified by a test, so that needs to be updated so that it doesn't catch the fix as an error.

issues.title: `cmd_close` silently no-ops on an already closed issue.
issues.description: When the `close` command on a closed issue, the program touches the issue, creating an update, and then reports a successful close.  The correct behavior would be to report that the issue is already closed and not touch it.

issues.title: There's another fixed width that collides with a derived value in `id_w`
issues.description: The issue is at `main.rs:161-172`, and are the same value encoded as dynamic in one spot, and fixed in another.  Better to make sure that they don't conflict in the future.

issues.title: `normalize_labels` does not de-dupe on on create or replace
issues.description: The `add-label` command does deduplication, but the other commands don't.  Unify the behavior to always deduplicate.

issues.title: No locking; concurrent tool invocations cause a race condition and data loss.
issues.description: We need to add a write lock to properly order scripted writes and avoid data loss.  Distinct from atomic writes, this is about multiple full writes racing each other.

issues.title: Temp file on the read-error path isn't cleaned up.
issues.description: This is a case where we need to use the proper Rust idiom for tempfile cleanup because the editor-failure path cleans up after itself automatically, but other errors don't.  This leaves orphaned files in /tmp.

issues.title: Predictable temp path in a shared directory.
issues.description: The temp files created by opening a description in an editor are named predictably, which means that they could be pre-emptively symlinked, and cause issues.  There's also the issue where this can cause collisions.  There's an idiomatic fix ni `tempfile::NamedTempFile` and we should use it.

issues.title: DESIGN.md is out of date in significant ways.
issues.description: The design doc is out of date because I used it as the starting point, and haven't updated it.  The changes are partially documented in PROCESS.md, and the actualy work is saved in the tracker log itself.  DESIGN.md is a living document to give the agents context for the current state, and to top it off, there's no basic documentation of the tool without digging through the `--help` options.

issues.title: No README for the project.
issues.description: This project needs a README to explain the basic functions and lay out the current state.  While this is a high priority, it should only be tackled once the features are stable.  Save until all the other issues for this round of work are handled.

issues.title: No way to remove a single label from an issue.
issues.description: There's no `--label-remove` to remove a single label, it's all or nothing.  Since the rest of the ergonomics for the labels are implemented, we should finish this last little issue.

issues.title: The tab complete for `-p` isn't working.
issues.description: In my use inputting all these issues, the tab completion for the priority levels doesn't work during the create workflow.

issues.title: Empty label filter fails silently instead of erroring.
issues.description: The label write rejects empty labels being written, but the filter for reading issues doesn't.  Make them match.

issues.title: Filter normalization is ad hoc, and not consistent across read/write ops.
issues.description: Like issue 42, this is another inconsistency between read and write.  Labels are trimmed on write, but not on read.  This means that an extra space on the list filter will error and find no issues.  All read and write ops should share the same input validation for consistency, if possible.

issues.title: `close` has a first class command, but reopen doesn't.
issues.description: This is confusing to the user because it's a one-shot to close an issue, but you have to use `update --status open` to reopen a closed issue.  Not only that, but that's the **only** valid way to do that.  I'm considering a first class `reopen` command, and _possibly_ having that also move issues from `done` to `open`, if something wasn't quite finished, instead of having to round-trip it through `in-progress`.  Prompt for design discussion to review the logic here.

issues.title: `truncate_title` counts chars, not display columns.
issues.description: This is an issue for CJK characters, and is easily fixable with the `unicode-width` crate, it seems.

issues.title: Review test coverage for these additional cases.
issues.description: 1. No test asserts the list sort order actually puts critical above high or sinks done to the bottom — only the Ord impl is unit-tested (data.rs:169-174), not the rendered ordering in cmd_list (main.rs:428-435).  2. No test for the has_other_filter widening rule (main.rs:403-409) — i.e. that --priority high includes done but excludes closed. That branch encodes the trickiest requirement in the whole program (issue #7) and is untested end-to-end.  3. No test for close on an already-closed issue (bug #3 would have been caught).  4. No test for duplicate labels on create (bug #5).
